prerequisites: A solid background in physics, calculus and geometry

learning_outcomes.text: Deal with problems of static equilibrium and dynamics of planar and three-dimensional rigid bodies, in the presence of common types of constraints, friction and forces.
Recognize the physical meaning of the models adopted and the scope of applicability to derive equations of motion and stress characteristics.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental concepts of mechanics: forces, work, energy, power, ideal constraints, principle of constraint reactions, constraints with Coulomb friction.
Degrees of freedom of the point and of the rigid body in the plane.
Statics of the point, of systems of points, of the rigid body and of systems of rigid bodies, isostatic, hyperstatic and unrestrained conditions.
Geometry of masses and areas. Centres of mass, inertia tensor, diagonalisation (eigenvalue problem).
Introduction to the use of symbolic calculus (Mathematica).

Point and rigid body kinematics (in space). Rigid motions, coordinate transformations. Poisson formulas. Angular velocity. Relative motions. Centres of instantaneous rotation. Actual motion. Polars of motion.
Point and rigid body dynamics (in the plane) and applications of friction. Motion-quiet transition, inclined plane. Rolling.
Models of structural elements: beam, slab, shell, 3D models. Stress characteristics in beams and related diagrams.
Reticular structures, frames, machines and mechanisms.
assessment_rules: The grade is awarded by means of an overall assessment of the written paper and the homework completed and handed in within the allotted deadlines. Indicatively, 20 points will be allocated to the written test and 10 points to the homework assignments. The completion of the homework is not compulsory. In the absence of homework, the student can aspire to a maximum mark of 20/30. Any gaps on parts of the syllabus cannot be made up by answering additional questions on other parts of the syllabus. If preparation with gaps is established, the examination cannot be passed.
